findings.title: CAUTION overstates when the rolling-updates feature must be enabled
findings.body: The new CAUTION says: "While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail." Read literally this tells every reader that any deployment without the preview feature will break, but that is only true when an explicit update strategy is configured. With the default (unset) `spec.update.strategy` the Operator mimics 26.1 behavior and never invokes the update-compatibility command, so it works fine without the feature — this PR's own UpgradeTest demonstrates it: `createInitialDeployment` returns early for the null strategy without enabling `rolling-updates`, and `testCacheMaxCount(null)` still expects a successful rolling-upgrade status. The statement should be scoped (e.g., "must be enabled when configuring `spec.update.strategy`"), otherwise users on the default strategy may wrongly conclude they must enable a preview feature to keep the Operator working.

findings.title: New and changed update-compatibility exit codes are never asserted
findings.body: This PR introduces a new exit code (FEATURE_DISABLED = 4, returned when `rolling-updates` is not enabled) and changes the recreate exit code from 4 to 3 in CompatibilityResult, and the update-compatibility guide explicitly tells users to build automation around these exit codes rather than log output. However, no test verifies them: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the stderr message (line 49) and never checks that the process exits with code 4, and `testWrongVersions`/`testCompatible` assert messages but never assert exit code 3 (recreate required) or 0 (rolling possible) for the `check` command. A future regression that swaps or drops these exit codes — the tool's documented scripting contract — would pass the test suite unnoticed. Please add exitCode assertions to these tests.
